question.problem:
Which of the following products is the LU factorization of a matrix $A?$

I. $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -9 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$

II. $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}]$

III. $A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 6 & 1\end{aligned}]$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that in the LU factorization of a matrix $A,$ we write $A=LU$ where the matrix $L$ is a unit lower triangular matrix (a lower triangular matrix that has only $1$'s on the main diagonal) and the matrix $U$ is an upper triangular matrix:

$$
A=\overset{L}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ ∗ & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot \overset{U}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ \\ 0 & ∗\end{aligned}]}}
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each product in turn.

- The first product is in $LU$ form because the left matrix is a unit lower triangular matrix, and the right matrix is an upper triangular matrix.

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -9 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\,✓
$$

- The second product is in $LU$ form because the left matrix is a unit lower triangular matrix, and the right matrix is an upper triangular matrix.

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}]\,✓
$$

- The third product is *not* in $LU$ form. Although we have a product of an upper triangular matrix on the left and a unit lower triangular matrix on the right, the order of multiplication is not correct (instead, we need a unit lower triangular matrix on the left and an upper triangular matrix on the right).

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 6 & 1\end{aligned}]\,\times 
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".
